name: Downward Dog
intro:
Downward Dog (Adho Mukha Svanasana) is a widely practiced yoga pose known for its ability to stretch, strengthen, and energize the entire body. In this posture, the body forms an inverted V-shape, with hands and feet grounded while the hips lift upward. This position helps lengthen the spine, release tension, and improve overall flexibility.

This pose is commonly included in yoga sequences like Surya Namaskar and serves as both a strengthening and resting posture. It enhances blood circulation, especially towards the upper body and brain, which helps improve focus and mental clarity. The gentle inversion also supports relaxation while keeping the body active.

Regular practice of Downward Dog strengthens the arms, shoulders, and legs while stretching the hamstrings, calves, and back muscles. It is especially beneficial for reducing stiffness, improving posture, and boosting energy levels. This pose is ideal for people looking to build strength while also maintaining flexibility and balance in their daily routine.

steps.text: Start on your hands and knees with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
Spread your fingers wide and press your palms firmly into the mat.
Lift your hips upward, straightening your legs as much as comfortable.
Keep your head relaxed between your arms and look towards your feet.
Press your heels gently towards the ground without forcing.

benefits: Improves flexibility in hamstrings, calves, and spine
Enhances blood circulation to the brain
Calms the mind and reduces stress
Supports overall body balance and coordination
avoid: You have wrist injuries or severe shoulder pain
You are suffering from high blood pressure (consult a doctor before practice)
You have severe back injuries or spinal issues
You feel dizziness during the pose
You have recent surgery in arms, shoulders, or legs
You have glaucoma or eye pressure issues
You experience discomfort while holding the position
